thread:
jess: Heads-up — during the staging canary yesterday the cosign signer failed with a permission denied from KMS. Not a showstopper but it left a few images unsigned and triggered the rollback. Need to align on RBAC + audit logging before we flip prod rebuilds.
samir: ugh. which KMS key? staging or shared signer key?
emily: staging key only. error shows: `permissionDenied: serviceAccount=signer@redwood-staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com` in KMS audit logs.
mike: did deploy-bot surface the failure? @deploy-bot any logs?
deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-18T21:40Z — image-sign step failed (exit 1). See: https://ci.redwood/internal/builds/44923
jess: linked the build. The signer SA used to have roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier, but looks like a policy change removed iam.serviceAccounts.actAs for the pipeline invoker.
samir: so pipeline can't impersonate signer SA -> KMS call fails. We should rotate to short-lived signer creds and minimize actAs scope.
emily: agree. Proposal: create a dedicated signer workload identity per-cluster and give it only the KMS cryptoKeyVersions.useToSign permission + cosign verify minimal roles. No broad actAs outside the pipeline.
sec-oncall: checklist reminder: any RBAC change must be accompanied by synchronous audit logging enabled and an entry in the key access timeline. We need to ensure those KMS audit logs are exported to the long-term audit bucket before making changes.
jess: right. Two action items: (1) emergency preflight to restore pipeline impersonation so prod rebuilds can continue, (2) longer-term least-priv design + audit export and test-signer rollout.
mike: for (1) I can grant iam.serviceAccounts.actAs back to the CI runner group for signer SA temporarily. Need OK from security for timeboxed window.
samir: keep window short — 2 hours max. We should also attach an audit alert to detect subsequent actAs grants.
emily: also noticed a small gap: SBOMs for a subset of images didn't match after rebuild due to selinux label differences. That triggered our vuln triage flow and slowed canary.
jess: note that in the incident notes. We should add a GH issue to track deterministic SBOM generation across base-image patches.
sec-oncall: add to incident channel? we should treat the unsigned-image event as P2 until signer permissions are hardened and audit export is confirmed.
mike: ok I'm going to run the temporary grant now and post the IAM change in the audit-channel. ETA 5m.
emily: when you do, can you also run a quick cosign sign test against the staging key? e.g.

```
COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL=1 cosign sign --key gcpkms://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/staging/cryptoKeys/cosign/cryptoKeyVersions/1 \ 
  gcr.io/redwood-staging/my-service:canary
```

mike: on it.
deploy-bot: test-sign job started 2026-03-18T21:53Z
mike: test-sign succeeded, cosign signature present, KMS audit entry shows signer SA -> cryptoKeyVersion.useToSign.
samir: good. Next: who owns the rollout plan for switching to per-cluster WiD? @jess
jess: I'll draft a short migration plan: - create per-cluster signer WI - deploy signer sidecar for ephemeral keys - update CI to use WI-bound token - run canary signing across 3 clusters - enable KMS audit export
emily: include steps for SBOM normalization (strip file mtimes and stable ordering) and a test harness for attestation comparison.
sec-oncall: add to the plan: verify logs reach retention-longevity bucket and configure alert: "cosign-sign-failure" -> pager after 2 failures in 30m.
jess: assigning tasks: mike -> emergency IAM revert + documented timebound grant; samir -> the WI terraform modules; emily -> SBOM normalization PR and cosign test harness; me -> rollout doc + gating checklist.
mike: noted. I'll post update when the IAM grant window closes and attach the audit link.
emily: thanks. one more ask: should we rotate the staging cosign key after this incident?
samir: probably yes. rotation + re-attest older images. We'll need to coordinate a re-signing window and notify prod owners.
jess: add re-signing/rotation as a dependent step in the rollout doc. If anyone sees oddities, ping here or #incidents. :thumbsup:
